text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of working on a project all at once, teams use iterative development. This means they build the product in small, manageable pieces. Work is organized into short cycles called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. At the start of each sprint, the team selects tasks from a list called a backlog, which contains all the features that need to be built. These features are often described as user stories, which are short, simple explanations of a software feature from the end user's perspective. To keep everyone on track, the team holds a quick daily meeting known as a standup, where each member shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any obstacles in their way. This continuous feedback and adjustment allow teams to respond quickly to changes and deliver value regularly.
